I don't have any notes on Isaiah 50 for you yet. My first attempt to open the source pages was blocked: the tool said I'd used up my tool calls for this turn before any page loaded. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, so I haven't written anything from memory.

Next turn, I'll read these pages first:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word on Isaiah 50, plus Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Isaiah 50 at biblehub.com, and Precept Austin's Isaiah 50 page.
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes on Isaiah 50, and Bible Odyssey on the "Servant Songs" (Isaiah 50:4–9 is the third).
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's *Explanatory Notes* (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon's sermons on "set my face like flint" (v. 7) and on "walks in darkness and has no light" (vv. 10–11), and Ligonier, Desiring God and LCMS on the Servant as Christ.
- **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** Catholic and Orthodox pages on Isaiah 50:4–7 as a Holy Week and Palm Sunday reading.
- **Popular modern teaching:** anything the allowed sites say about "the tongue of the learned" (v. 4) and "words of faith."

Once I've read them, I'll write the notes verse by verse, give the URL for each point and leave out anything I can't find. Reply "go ahead" and I'll start.
